verdict.rationale: Pulumi's MCP server explicitly lets AI coding assistants (Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Claude Desktop) 'generate infrastructure code' from natural language, and Neo lets users 'tell it what you need in plain English' (e.g., 'Give me a VPC with a subnet in every AZ') to provision infrastructure. This is native, first-party AI tooling built into the Pulumi ecosystem, not a third-party bolt-on. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on validation of code-generation quality (community commentary on Pulumi's genAI docs being weak suggests some real-world friction) and more detail on how generated code integrates back into the standard IaC workflow.
